heading: What OpenWiki actually is
content: OpenWiki is a TypeScript CLI that writes and maintains documentation for a codebase, built to be read by other coding agents. It's a LangChain-ecosystem tool (deepagents + langchain/@langchain/*) that runs an LLM-driven documentation agent against a target repo and produces/maintains a tree of Markdown docs under openwiki/ in that repo. Three modes: --init (generate from scratch), --update (refresh based on git diff since last run), chat (interactive), -p/--print (one-shot). It self-installs a pointer block into the host repo's AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md so other agents know to read openwiki/quickstart.md first. This checkout is a downstream fork (origin -> c10vis-poem/openwiki), not vanilla upstream langchain-ai/openwiki -- it adds a project-scoped openwiki/SKILL.md framed in-repo as 'memory as a skill' and called the fork's focal architecture.

heading: Repository structure
content: CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md are identical pointer files ('docs live in /openwiki, start at openwiki/quickstart.md'). README.md covers install/usage/customization including the SKILL.md convention. DEVELOPMENT.md has local dev/link instructions (pnpm). openwiki/ is the generated wiki itself: quickstart.md, architecture/overview.md, agent/workflow.md, cli/usage.md, operations/credentials-and-updates.md, SKILL.md, .last-update.json. src/ holds the actual CLI/agent source: cli.tsx (Ink UI, run lifecycle), commands.ts (argv parsing), credentials.tsx (onboarding), env.ts (~/.openwiki/.env persistence), constants.ts (provider configs, path constants), agent/index.ts (agent runtime/model creation), agent/prompt.ts (system/user prompt assembly -- the actual maintenance rulebook), agent/utils.ts (git evidence + content-hash snapshot + metadata writes), agent/types.ts (shared types). .github/workflows/checks.yml runs lint/format CI; examples/openwiki-update.yml is a copyable scheduled-update GitHub Action.

heading: The schema/config layer for wiki maintenance
content: Two layered mechanisms govern wiki maintenance. First, CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md -- a generic, auto-inserted pointer block any agent reads first, templated in src/agent/prompt.ts around lines 92-105. Second, openwiki/SKILL.md -- a per-repo, optional, project-scoped override file read on every run (chat, --init, --update), enforced by createProjectSkillSection() in src/agent/prompt.ts. It layers project conventions/terminology/scope on top of built-in behavior without forking OpenWiki's own code, described in-repo as 'memory as a skill.' It cannot override security rules or the 'only write inside openwiki/' restriction. The actual maintenance rulebook lives in createSystemPrompt()/createModeInstructions() in src/agent/prompt.ts -- governs structure (quickstart-first, at most 8 pages on init, no thin stub pages/directories), git-evidence discipline, subagent fan-out rules, and a 'surgical update' policy (edit only pages tied to real diffs, don't touch source maps/formatting).

heading: Memory / retrieval / RAG / MCP surface -- none present
content: OpenWiki has no vector store, embeddings, RAG, or MCP anywhere in this repo, confirmed via repo-wide grep for websocket|embedding|RAG|retriev|MCP|vector|memory (only hits are the SKILL.md 'memory as a skill' prose). Persistence primitives that do exist: a SQLite checkpointer (~/.openwiki/openwiki.sqlite via @langchain/langgraph-checkpoint-sqlite) persisting LangGraph conversation threads for chat continuity, not a knowledge base; openwiki/.last-update.json holding run metadata (updatedAt, command, gitHead, model) used to scope incremental doc updates; a content-hash snapshot (createOpenWikiContentSnapshot() in src/agent/utils.ts, SHA-256 over the openwiki/ tree) to detect no-op updates; DeepAgents LocalShellBackend (virtualMode: true, repo-rooted virtual filesystem) as the agent execution substrate, with no MCP or external tool integration beyond LangChain model providers (Anthropic/OpenAI/OpenRouter/Baseten/Fireworks). Optional LangSmith tracing exists for observability only, not memory.

heading: Testing and tooling conventions
content: There are no test files at all in this repo -- no unit or integration test suite. Quality gates are purely static: .github/workflows/checks.yml runs pnpm run format:check (Prettier) and pnpm run lint:check (ESLint/typescript-eslint) on PRs. Build is tsc via pnpm run build; dev loop is tsx src/cli.tsx or OPENWIKI_DEV=1 openwiki --dry-run.

heading: Extensibility as a base/fork layer for a larger system
content: Two concrete extension points make OpenWiki plausible as a base for forking: (1) openwiki/SKILL.md, already designed as a generic per-project customization hook read on every run and explicitly marketed as 'memory as a skill' -- the natural seam for injecting behavioral rules from other systems like OB1 or reasoning-bank without touching src/; (2) the src/constants.ts provider abstraction (PROVIDER_CONFIGS, OpenWikiProvider type, createModel() branch in src/agent/index.ts) -- a clean, centralized pattern for adding new backends/model sources, mirrorable for adding new memory backends or transport channels. However, OpenWiki's core loop is narrowly a doc-generation CLI: git-evidence-driven, file-snapshot-gated, LangGraph/DeepAgents-specific, with no runtime API/server, no WebSocket, no HTTP server, and no plugin/hook system today. Fork-basing on it gets you the prompt-discipline/doc-structure conventions, the SKILL.md memory-layering convention, and the metadata/snapshot pattern for incremental updates -- but a websocket/frontend interface layer would be entirely new code, likely living beside src/cli.tsx (currently an Ink TUI, not a server).
